description: A bright-field transmission electron micrograph of deformed Fe–28% Al, presented as a montage of three overlapping fields of view (left, centre, right) that together form a wide-area view of the dislocation substructure. Contrast is dark-line dislocation contrast against a light grey matrix, with darker banded regions (bend/ extinction contours and foil-thickness variations) crossing the fields. A black scale bar in the lower-right corner is labelled "0.5µm", and directly above it a black arrow points toward the upper-left, marking the direction of the imaging vector g. The dislocation population is dense and roughly uniformly distributed: most lines are long and markedly straight, others kink and bow, and many are arranged in parallel pairs, in loose tangles along the lower-left to upper-right diagonal, or in rectangular network/junction configurations near the centre and right (including a group of closely spaced parallel straight segments in the upper-right field). The caption states the zone axis is near [0 0 1] and the arrowed imaging vector is 2 0 0, so this image displays the superdislocation array of Fe–28% Al in which straight, near-screw-oriented lines dominate. No numeric dislocation counts or densities are printed.

observations.observation: The figure is a bright-field TEM micrograph montage of three overlapping fields showing dark-line dislocation contrast on a light grey matrix.
A black scale bar in the lower-right corner is labelled '0.5µm'.
A black arrow above the scale bar points toward the upper-left, marking the direction of the imaging vector g.

Most dislocations visible are long and generally straight, with some bowed or kinked segments; several parallel line pairs and rectangular network/junction configurations are present, particularly in the centre and right fields.
No numeric dislocation density, Burgers vector magnitude or count is printed anywhere in the figure; the only printed quantity is the 0.5 µm scale bar.
The caption states the micrograph is of deformed Fe–28% Al and shows many superdislocations, generally straight and in near-screw orientations.
The caption states the zone axis is near [0 0 1] and that the arrowed imaging vector is 2 0 0.

The citing text states that the dislocations are now invariably superdislocations composed of two (1/2)111 partials, i.e. perfect superdislocations for the B2 lattice but imperfect for the DO3 lattice, trailing APBII faults as they glide.
The citing text states that Fig. 10 shows large numbers of rather straight superdislocations of several different Burgers vectors, often in near-screw orientations along their {110} glide planes.

The citing text states that examination of these superdislocations in +g and -g imaging conditions shows many arranged in dipole configurations (marked d in a later figure) while other pairs have identical Burgers vectors.
The image shows no g-vector label or zone-axis annotation overlaid on the pixels themselves; the zone axis and g = 2 0 0 are supplied only by the caption.

subfigures.description: Left field of the bright-field TEM montage: a light matrix with a few long straight dark dislocation lines and short curved segments, plus faint bend contours and small dark dot-like defects near the lower edge.
Centre overlapping field: the highest density of long dislocation lines, many of them straight and parallel, together with curved/bowed lines and dark banded contrast running diagonally.

Right field: sparse long curved dislocations, several rectangular/network junction configurations, and a conspicuous cluster of closely spaced parallel straight line segments (a dipole/ribbon-like group) near the centre of this field.
Black horizontal scale bar labelled '0.5µm' with a black arrow immediately above it pointing toward the upper-left, indicating the direction of the imaging (diffraction) vector g.
subfigures.panel: scale bar and g arrow (lower right)

unreadable_items: No crystallographic labels (zone axis, g = 2 0 0, diffraction pattern inset) are printed within the image; these are only given in the caption
The exact azimuthal angle of the arrowed g vector relative to the dislocation line directions cannot be measured from the pixels
Individual dislocation Burgers vectors cannot be distinguished from this single bright-field image
